result.description:
Just Better Care Eastern Suburbs

Full-Time Disabilities Services Officer (Multiple positions)

About us:
Just Better Care provides in-home disability and aged care services, supporting people to live independently. We believe people of all ages & all abilities deserve access to the support and resources they need in order to live where they want and how they want. At Just Better Care, we CARE about our customers and our team. Our office covers four territories in the Sydney Metro area; Eastern Suburbs, Inner West, Sutherland and St George.
Just Better Care Eastern Suburb is looking for Disabilities Services Officer to join our caring and dynamic team. This role involves working with customers to support them in many different aspects of their day-to-day life. The role involves supporting customers with mental, physical, social and emotional disabilities. Support is provided in a manner that maintains the customer’s independence, is respectful and safe.

Main responsibility
• Demonstrate a commitment to best practice, ensuring that all services are provided in a caring and respectful way in accordance with Just Better Care’s policy and procedures.
• Assessing clients' needs and developing individual support plans
• Social support/transportation: social activities, shopping/groceries, travelling to medical appointments
• Clinical support: medication assistance
• Supporting customers in the use of aids and personal equipment including: standing or walking frames, wheelchairs, manual or electric hoists, sliding sheets or moving boards, hearing aids and other physical aids
• Supporting customers with complex and/or challenging behaviours
• Monitoring the well-being of customers and reporting on their progress
• Providing a safe environment for the client by monitoring their surroundings for potential dangers such as fire hazards and tripping hazards.
• Supporting clients socially and arranging visits or outings in the community.
• Ensuring that all documentation is completed in a timely and accurate manner. Where offices are using Mobility Options, community support workers are required to use the application for all schedule visits as per their training.
• Attending and participating in staff meetings and training sessions as directed by the Coordinator.
• Ensuring that all responsible steps are taken to protect personal safety at work and avoid adversely affecting the health or safety of any other person at the workplace in accordance with requirements under the Work Health and Safety legalisation.
• Participating in activities aimed at the continuous improvement of services.
• Complying with Just Better Care’s Vision, Values, and Purpose

What you will need:
• Qualification in the relevant field.
• At least 2 years’ relevant work experience.
• NDIS Workers Check or Police Clearance
• Current Australian Drivers Licence
• Current First Aid and CPR certificates
• Ability to be contacted by either telephone or email
• Ability or willingness to assist or work with customer in daily living and personal care skills
• Be reliable & productive
• Valuing attitudes towards customers
• Ability to work as part of a Team and maintain good working relationships
• Commitment to self-improvement
• Good written and verbal skills in English

Salary Range: $80,000 to 90,000 per annum excluding superannuation.
Why Join Us:
• Close-knit team of friendly, helpful and supportive people.
• Career development and training opportunities are very high on our priority list.
• We have a vested interest in you, hence you will be well supported.
• A competitive salary is on offer for the right candidate.
• Employee Assistance Programme.
If you have any questions or would like to know more about the role, send an e-mail to hr.es@justbettercare.com

Irrigation Technician
Employer:Rita's Farm Produce Pty Limited
Location: 1204 Mamre Road, Kemps Creek, NSW 2178, Australia
Employment type: Full-time, 38 hours per week
Remuneration: $75,000 - $85,000 

About Rita Farm
Since its establishment in 2001, Rita's Farm Produce Pty Limited has been deeply engaged in Australia's organic agriculture sector for over 20 years. It is a highly reputable certified organic family farm in New South Wales, located at 1204 Mamre Road, Kemps Creek, covering an area of 55 acres. Adhering to strict organic farming standards, the farm consistently upholds the core philosophy of "growing food as medicine" and is committed to providing high-quality organic fruits, vegetables, and baked goods—free of chemical pesticides and synthetic fertilizers—to Sydney, Canberra, and surrounding regions.
We adhere to sustainable agricultural practices and protect biodiversity through ecological balance technologies, having now become a benchmark brand in the local organic agriculture sector. To support the farm's large-scale development and the refined management of its irrigation systems, we are sincerely inviting professional irrigation technicians to join us in jointly safeguarding the core lifeline of organic farming.

Duties & Responsibilities
System Operation & Maintenance Management: Responsible for the daily operation, inspection, maintenance, and troubleshooting of drip/sprinkler irrigation systems (including water pumps, pipelines, etc.), ensuring the precise irrigation needs of 55 acres of organic crops are met.
Irrigation Plan Development: Develop scientific irrigation plans based on organic standards, crop cycles, soil, and climate data. Precisely control water volume and frequency to ensure certification compliance.
Fertigation Integration Operation: Operate relevant equipment to precisely mix organic fertilizers for simultaneous irrigation. Monitor the process and record data to ensure efficient nutrient absorption.
Data Optimization & Review: Establish operation records for irrigation systems, documenting equipment status, test data, etc. Regularly analyze efficiency and propose optimization or upgrade suggestions.
Safety & Collaboration Assurance: Adhere to WHS (Work Health and Safety) standards. Coordinate with the planting team and farm manager to provide irrigation technical support and participate in planting planning meetings.

Selection Criteria / Skills & Qualifications
Possess 1-3 years of relevant experience in irrigation system installation/maintenance, or practical experience in horticultural/agricultural irrigation.
Proficient in the operation and maintenance of core irrigation system components, including pumps, valves, piping, and irrigation controllers, with a solid understanding of water supply scheduling logic.
Have a basic grasp of the principles of hydraulic parameters in agricultural/horticultural settings and an understanding of water resource optimization and management methods.
Adaptable to outdoor working environments, capable of independently completing physical work tasks, and equipped with reliable maintenance execution capabilities.
Demonstrate strong communication and coordination skills, able to effectively collaborate with farm teams and management.
Meticulous and reliable in work, prioritize work safety, strictly comply with labour hire industry standards, and adhere to high-quality craftsmanship requirements.
Flexible to adjust work arrangements in line with the farm’s production cycles.

What We Offer
Competitive salary for a full-time, 38-hour week role.
Stable employment with compliant labour-hire arrangements, including rostered hours, structured workforce management, and professional work conditions aligned with our values of integrity, reliability, and compliance.

More information
For more information, please email(adding company email). To learn more about working with us, we encourage you to visit our website
https://www.ritasfarm.com.au/

1204 Mamre Road, Kemps Creek, NSW 2178, Australia

Visa sponsorship

We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




An exciting opportunity to join the Child and Youth HOPE Team as a wellbeing support worker!









Work within a dynamic, multidisciplinary team












 Based at Cranbourne Community Hospital 












Assertive outreach to support young people and their families










Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives.







About the Department - Program






The CY-HOPE team provides wellbeing-psychosocial support, peer support and brief clinical support to young people in the 0-18 age range presenting with suicide and self-harm concerns. The Wellbeing Support Worker will work as part of the CY-HOPE team under its governance and support and, as such, will have opportunities to work in a variety of community settings.







About the Team






The Infant, Child and Youth Area Mental Health & Wellbeing Service provides assessment and treatment for infants, children, adolescents, young people and their families. We work with the 0-18 age in the Southern Region. We provide a comprehensive assessment service and a range of treatment options including inpatient treatment in times of crisis, community (outpatient) treatment, group programs, family therapy, and specialist services.






The Child & Youth Hospital Outreach Post-Suicidal Engagement (CY-HOPE) Team is a core component of Victoria's suicide prevention framework, which aimed to halve Victoria's suicide rate by 2025. This new service gives children and young people who are intentionally self-harming, experiencing suicidal ideation, or have attempted suicide a rapid and intensive form of support that is designed to prevent rate of recurrence and ultimately reduce rates of suicide among children and young people. Importantly, this includes engagement and support of their parents-carers, families and extended support networks in assertive outreach provided.






All stakeholders (children, young people, their parents-carers, families and service providers) will work together in this Child and Youth HOPE service at the Infant, Child and Youth Area Mental Health & Wellbeing Service at Monash Health. This service has been co-designed with and for young people and carers, First Nations people, people from Culturally Diverse Communities, LGBTIQ+ people, people in Out of Home Care, and Neurodivergent people.






The co-designed service goals are: Approachable & Accessible, Positive & Empowering, Empathetic & Personalised, Responsible & Accountable, Creative & Resourceful, and Connected & Cohesive. Infant, Child and Youth Area Mental Health & Wellbeing Service provides assessment and treatment for infants, children, adolescents, young people and their families. We work with the 0-18 age in the Southern Region. We provide a comprehensive assessment service and a range of treatment options including inpatient treatment in times of crisis, community (outpatient) treatment, group programs, family therapy, and specialist services.







About the Role






Join our team as a wellbeing support worker on a part time (0.8), fixed term (30 June 2027, with potential for this to be extended), to work at Cranbourne Community Hospital based at Cranbourne East. In this role, you will be guided under the leadership of the Team Manager and working with the broader CY-HOPE team. 


Monash Health is excited to announce a Wellbeing Support Worker position in the Child & Youth Hospital Outreach Post-Suicidal Engagement (CY-HOPE) Team with the Infant, Child and Youth Area Mental Health & Wellbeing Service.






The Wellbeing Support Workers are the key workers for the young people in the CY-HOPE Team. They carry a caseload of 10 young people and provide non-clinical psychosocial support to young people and their families. This may include:









supporting engaging with friends, family, school, community programs












developing independent life skills












liaising with and supporting referrals to other mental health supports and-or family support services.












A combination of clinic based and outreach appointments









They work alongside the mental health clinicians, peer workers and consultant psychiatrist in the CY-HOPE Team to provide a meaningful approach to care that assists the young person to stay safe and connect with essential services in the first 12 weeks following discharge from hospital or contact with the service after a suicide attempt or a suicidal crisis.






The 0.8 EFT position will require you to work on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, with the other day to be of your choosing.







About You






To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience, and attributes:









Experienced in mental health support, and-or child and family welfare support.












Strong values about the central role of the lived experience workforce, wellbeing support, and co-design in mental health service development and delivery.












Strong values about inclusion and diversity. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.












Person centred focus, emphasis on providing choice and flexibility. Expected to be enthusiastic, compassionate & able to work collaboratively, able to prioritise and meet deadlines.












Be autonomous in work organisation and time management. Be adept in problem solving and is a solution focused person.

Provide valid proof of your current right to work in Australia.

result.description:
Full-time Wall and Floor Tiler position available with a competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Hurlstone Park, NSW 2193

•	Full-Time Position
•	$80,000 - $90,000 plus superannuation 
•	Operate within a professional setting.

FerMax Stone Pty Ltd is an Australian company established in 2012, specialising in the installation of premium wall and floor tiling, natural stone, porcelain and other high-quality surface finishes for residential and commercial projects. Since its establishment, the company has built a reputation for delivering quality workmanship, reliability and exceptional customer service across a wide range of projects.
On behalf of our client, we are looking for an experienced and skilled Wall and Floor tiler to join our team on a full-time basis

Position Responsibilities and Tasks

As a Wall and Floor Tiler, your duties will include, but will not be limited to:

•	Interpret plans and specifications; confirm measurements, quantities, layout lines and levels prior to commencing tiling works.
•	Measure, mark and set out surfaces using levelling equipment (including laser levels) to establish correct alignment, falls and datum lines.
•	Measure, cut, shape and install custom heritage mosaic tiles and decorative stone finishes, ensuring accurate pattern alignment, preserving heritage design features and delivering high-quality workmanship in accordance with project specifications.
•	Prepare wall and floor substrates by removing old tiles, grout and adhesives; filling holes and cracks; and cleaning/priming surfaces to ensure suitable adhesion and finish.
•	Lay and fix tiles (including ceramic, clay, slate, marble, glass and similar materials) to internal and external walls and floors to achieve required patterns, alignment and tolerances.
•	Apply adhesives and bedding materials to substrates and/or tile backs as required, ensuring correct coverage, bonding and curing in line with product specifications.
•	Cut, shape and fit tiles using hand and power tile-cutting tools to finish edges, corners and penetrations around fittings, pipes and fixtures.
•	Maintain consistent alignment and spacing throughout installation, checking for lippage, level, line and falls, and adjusting as required during installation.
•	Complete grouting, finishing and clean-down, including removing excess grout and presenting a consistent, defect-free surface finish.
•	Support waterproofing outcomes by assisting with waterproofing preparation/detailing and coordinating tiling works with waterproofing stages and inspection hold points, ensuring correct detailing at junctions and penetrations in wet areas and external areas.
•	Undertake substrate preparation activities that support tiling quality (e.g., grinding, levelling and surface preparation), and coordinate transitions/interfaces with epoxy or other protective floor finishes where required by project scope.
•	Work collaboratively on major construction sites across Sydney/NSW, liaising with site foremen and project managers regarding sequencing, access, quality inspections and program timeframes.
•	Maintain compliance with WHS requirements, including safe manual handling, correct PPE use, silica dust controls and safe operation of plant and tools used for cutting and surface preparation.


Qualifications and Skills:

•	Certificate III in Wall and Floor Tiling or relevant trade qualification.
•	At least two years of relevant experience.
•	Sound knowledge of wall and floor tiling techniques and installation methods.
•	Experience working with ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite and natural stone products.
•	Ability to read and interpret plans and technical drawings.
•	Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality workmanship.

Salary:
The role offers a remuneration package of $80,000 - $90,000 per annum, plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

result.description:
As a Service Technician, you will provide professional support to our customers through mechanical troubleshooting, overhauls, repair, service and reporting of spark ignition natural gas engines, compressor and controls issues. Your innate ability to produce high volume, quality output, coupled with a natural ability to build meaningful relationships are key pillars for success in this role.

Your day-to-day includes:

· Perform timely and efficient mechanical troubleshooting, repairs and service to customer equipment in remote environments.

· Provide clear accurate technical advice and economical solutions to challenges in the field including assisting clients with maintenance strategies to improve reliability of plant and equipment.

· Provide clear and concise reports on work completed in order to indicate to the customer work performed and any future work or process recommendations.

· Maintain a high level of QHSE awareness sand encourage participation among fellow employees in the assessment of risks & monitoring the progress of HSE performance. Immediately report all Health, Safety and Environment incidents to your manager.

· Maintain company tooling and equipment on site and in the workshop to an above average standard of use at all times.

· Assist with the identification of continuous improvement opportunities and participate in the development and implementation of solutions.

· Equipment failure analysis and reporting.

· Ability to multi-task and work autonomously.

· Accept responsibility for your workmanship and the development of positive customer relations.

· Demonstrate a willingness and capability to perform other duties as deemed appropriate and consistent with your professional qualifications, skill or experience.

Job Type: Permanent
Roster: 15 days on, 13 days off
Hours: 37.5 averaged hours per week over 4 weeks
Yearly Salary: $140,000 - $155,000 base per year

About us
Altrad is a trusted provider of expert construction and integrated maintenance solutions across Australia, with a strong track record across key sectors such as energy, mining, utilities, and defence. We are known for managing some of the nation's most critical projects.
We go beyond simply building, protecting, and extending asset life. We cultivate strong, collaborative partnerships with our clients, allowing us to tailor solutions to their evolving needs and ensure their assets operate seamlessly for longer.
We are part of the Altrad Group, a global organisation with nearly 52,000 people across more than 50 countries and 120 subsidiaries operating in Europe, the Americas, Canada, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia Pacific.
Why you should work for Altrad
We provide the benefits you’d expect from a global company, but what makes us different?

Our Opportunities: Embark on a thrilling journey with us, tackling diverse and exciting challenges on some of the world's most prominent resources, energy, and infrastructure projects.
Our Vibrant Culture: Immerse yourself in a dynamic atmosphere where problem-solving is a way of life. Join a reliable and enthusiastic team that thrives on a 'can-do' spirit, making every workday an opportunity for growth and collaboration.
Our Investment in You: Your success matters to us, and we're here to support your aspirations. Let us be your partner in reaching new heights and unlocking your full potential. Your journey to success starts here!
Our global workforce drives and promotes an inclusive culture, both within our organisation and throughout the communities we interact with across the world. Diverse backgrounds include First Nations Peoples, people with differing abilities, LGBTIQ+ community, gender, neurodiverse, cultural diversity, all age groups, and those with an intersectional or multiple diverse characteristics. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

How to Apply:
If you are a motivated and experienced Insulator looking for new opportunities, we would love to hear from you. Please submit your expression of interest along with your resume and relevant certifications by clicking on “Apply Now” or call Recruitment on 1300 142 806.
